title: The Anvil That Asked a Question
story: In the mountain forge, Orrinvex the Riddle Anvil has clamped shut on the smith's hammer and refuses to open for anything but a correct number. The village needs 7 identical horseshoe nails from every bar of iron, and the anvil speaks only in puzzles. Mr 6 leans in, curious rather than afraid.
question: Orrinvex growls: "A number of iron bars, times 7 nails each, gives 84 nails. Add 6 more bars to that number. What number do you now hold?"
hint: First find what number times 7 makes 84. Then do what the anvil says with that number.
victory: "Eighteen," said Mr 6, "and six of those are me, in a manner of speaking." Orrinvex laughed so hard it sprang open, and the hammer clanged happily to the floor.
imagePrompt: A massive iron anvil with a carved grinning face and glowing rune-eyes gripping a hammer in a red-lit mountain forge, with a small caped numeral 6 knight scratching sums into the soot.
solution: Find the starting number of bars: 84 ÷ 7 = 12 bars.
The anvil says add 6 more bars: 12 + 6 = 18.
praise: Nice work spotting that 7 and 84 belong together — dividing was exactly the right instinct, and the only missing step was adding the 6 extra bars at the end.
